answer.location_description: A full-image horizontal stripe (grating) pattern with a period of 4 rows. Pairs of rows alternate: rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 versus rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23. The pattern spans every column, including the corners far from the nodule.
answer.mechanism: Eight layer-1 units are horizontal-grating detectors in two opposite phases. Phase-B detectors (units 12, 13, 23, 29) have negative biases (-74, -72, -88, -56). Their weights are positive on rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9 and so on, and negative on rows 2-3, 6-7 and so on. A uniform image largely cancels, so they fire only when the stripe pattern is present. Phase-A units (2, 11, 17, 25) have the opposite sign pattern and large positive biases (74, 99, 81, 84), so they are on by default and are suppressed by phase-B stripes. In layer 2, phase-B units feed strongly into units that push the output toward malignant: u0 (W3 +85), u8 (+62), u10 (+76), u14 (+90). Example weights: u8 from unit 12 is +99, u10 from unit 23 is +82. Phase-A units feed the units that push toward benign, u9 (W3 -99) and u11 (W3 -66), and inhibit the malignant ones. Example weights: u14 from unit 17 is -87, u10 from unit 17 is -96. Net effect: bright horizontal lines at rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, ... raise the malignant logit.
answer.evidence: Units 2, 11, 12, 13, 17, 23, 25 and 29 are the only layer-1 units with large, structured weights; the other 24 units look like small random noise. In all eight, whole rows share the same sign and alternate every 2 rows across all 24 columns. Unit 12 is a clear example: r0-r1 are about +20 to +40, r2-r3 about -20 to -40, r4-r5 about +30 to +60, r6-r7 about -30 to -80, and so on down to r20-r21 at about +40. Unit 2 shows the exact opposite: r2-r3 and r6-r7 at about +30 to +70, r4-r5 at about -30 to -50. A pattern that is uniform across columns and extends into the image corners cannot be a property of a nodule centred and scaled in the crop; nodule features would be roughly radial and central. The layer-2 and layer-3 weights consistently route phase-B detectors to positive-logit units and phase-A detectors to negative-logit units.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the stripe detector, the model has only modest local modulations near the centre embedded in the same units. Examples are bright-region weights around rows 10-11, cols 16-19 and rows 14-15, cols 8-11, which plausibly respond to nodule density, size or shape. The malignancy decision appears dominated by the horizontal-stripe pattern rather than nodule morphology.
